text.p: Illness forced defending champion Thomas Enqvist of Sweden to retire from his first round match in the Indian Open tennis tournament at Madras on Wednesday.
The second-seeded Enqvist, ranked seventh in the world, conceded to Germany's 209th-ranked Rainer Schuttler at 6-6 in the first set as the crowd awaited the start of the tie-break.

Third-seeded American MaliVai Washington, the losing Wimbledon finalist last year, meanwhile overcame a sluggish start to beat Uzbekistan's Oleg Ogorodov 3-6 7-6 (7-3) 6-1 to reach the quarter-finals.
Joining him was fifth-seeded Alex Radulescu of Germany, ranked 58th, who scored a 6-4 7-5 second-round victory over 151st-ranked Fernon Wibier of Netherlands.

Enqvist was the second Swede to retire exhausted due to heat in the tournament on successive days. On Tuesday, Lars Jonsson had retired during the third set of his first round match against Italy's Marco Mengeschincheri.
"I have been having nausea for three days but was very keen to defend my title," Enqvist said. "Unfortunately I just could not continue."
The tournament doctor, Vece Paes, said Enqvist arrived in Madras feeling sick.
"He probably picked up a virus on his way here after playing the Davis Cup and the heat exhaustation aggravated his condition," Dr Paes said.
Sweden beat South Africa 3-2 in the Davis Cup quarterfinals last weekend.
